summary.title: FIT5163 Week 8 Lab
summary.description: MediTrack lab threat model: patients, doctors and administrators use a Web/API server for appointments and medical records. Reminders use a third-party SMS provider. Includes TB1-TB5 and the 10 worked STRIDE threats from the supplied lab. Controls are proposals, not implemented assurances.

diagrams.title: Week 8 - DFD

data.name: Patient
data.description: Patient browser. Log in, book/cancel appointments and view own medical records. Browser input is untrusted.

data.name: Doctor
data.description: Doctor browser. Access authorised patient records; create or update notes and prescriptions.

data.name: Admin
data.description: Receptionist/admin browser. Manage schedules and user accounts through the API; no direct store access or blanket medical-record access is assumed.

and messaging
data.description: Internal application functions of the same Web/API server. TB5 requires role and object authorisation on every action. Patient: own data; doctor: treating relationship; admin: schedules/accounts. Deny by default.

threats.title: Stored XSS or permissive CORS
threats.description: A malicious stored note/message can act in a doctor session; permissive credentialed CORS may expose the records API. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Apply contextual output encoding and CSP; use a strict CORS allow-list and never reflect arbitrary credentialed origins.

threats.title: Booking or API resource exhaustion
threats.description: Unbounded requests or bookings exhaust appointment slots or server resources. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use rate limits, per-account booking quotas and bounded execution timeouts.

data.privilegeLevel: Server-side least privilege; per-request role and object checks required

data.name:
Patients +
Appointments DB
data.description: Patient/account data and appointment schedules. DB queries must be parameterised at TB2. Encryption and credential-storage controls are requirements, not verified implemented controls.

threats.title: Password disclosure from database leak
threats.description: A leaked database reveals plaintext passwords or easily cracked fast hashes. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use salted Argon2id/scrypt/bcrypt hashes; encrypt sensitive data at rest and restrict database access.

data.name:
Medical records
store
data.description: Critical asset: patient health records, clinical notes and prescriptions. Every object read/write requires authorisation at TB3. Record changes require protected audit evidence.

data.name:
SMS provider
(third party)
data.description: External provider delivering appointment reminders to patients. Send only the phone number and minimum reminder details; never full medical records.

data.name: Session store
data.description: Server-side session IDs, user identity and expiry. Session data must be integrity-protected; tokens require strong randomness and controlled expiry.

data.name: TB1 - Internet / API
data.description: Untrusted browser requests enter the Web/API server. Authenticate, validate and authorise. Responses cross back to the browser. The full-height line separates the labelled zones and covers all related cross-boundary flows.

data.name: TB5 - Role / object checks
data.description: Logical privilege boundary inside the same Web/API server, not a network segment. Check Patient/Doctor/Admin permissions and object-level access for every action. The full-height line separates the labelled zones and covers all related cross-boundary flows.

data.name: TB2 - Database
data.description: Treat input as data, never executable SQL. Use a least-privileged database identity.

data.name: TB3 - Medical records
data.description: Patient health records are the critical asset. Authorise every record read and write.

data.name: TB4 - Third party
data.description: Phone numbers and minimal appointment reminder details leave the application trust zone.

data.name:

Session cookie and responses
data.description: Patient requests and corresponding responses. Encryption flags are not asserted because transport controls have not been verified.

threats.title: Session spoofing
threats.description: Stolen or guessable session cookies allow impersonation of a patient or doctor. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use CSPRNG session tokens, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, expiry and rotation; consider MFA.

threats.title: CSRF books or cancels appointments
threats.description: A forged cross-site request changes a booking using the victim session. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Require anti-CSRF tokens on state-changing requests and appropriate SameSite cookies.

threats.title: Prescription edits lack audit evidence
threats.description: A doctor edits a prescription and later denies the change when no protected audit trail exists. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Record who/what/when in append-only, tamper-protected audit logs for record/prescription changes.

threats.title: Patient invokes doctor or admin actions
threats.description: UI-only role restrictions allow a patient to call privileged endpoints directly. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Recheck server-side roles and object permissions on every restricted action; fail closed.

threats.title: SQL injection at TB2
threats.description: Attacker-controlled login or search input changes a database query. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterised queries/prepared statements and least-privileged database credentials.

threats.title: IDOR: access another patient record
threats.description: Changing a record or patient ID exposes records without object-level access checks. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Authorise each specific record read/write server-side; deny by default.

threats.title: Third-party reminder data exposure
threats.description: Phone numbers or appointment details are disclosed to or through the SMS provider. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Minimise reminder content, use TLS, review provider handling and establish a data-processing agreement.

diagrams.description: MediTrack DFD. The two Web/API process symbols decompose one server logically. TB1: Internet/API; TB2: database; TB3: records; TB4: SMS provider; TB5: role and object authorisation inside the API. No direct admin-to-database access is assumed. All threats remain Open; severity estimates require review. Revised: larger bidirectional arrowheads on seven request/response flows; SMS remains unidirectional. Authentication ports are separated to avoid overlapping arrowheads. TB1 and TB5 extend across the full working height and zones are labelled; authentication is not a guarantee that input is safe.
